body:
Well, they’ve done it. Governor Lee’s “special session” has ended and no surprises he got exactly what he wanted.

| | | | | [ ](https://zg05qvsd.r.us-east-2.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Fourtenn.org%2F/1/010f0194b9a9fedf-6656d8e0-bf06-4e44-86e3-50d3d91507b3-000000/zPKgWAf-K9yBsg-cMQRL629uVpY=195)
---
Hello Peter,
---
| | Well, they’ve done it. Governor Lee’s “special session” has ended and no surprise he got exactly what he wanted.
Just as we expected, Speaker Sexton and the rest of the extremist Republicans have sold out our kids and passed Governor Lee’s voucher scam 54-44. This program will rip money away from our public schools and funnel it to special interests.
And that’s not all. In the Tennessee Legislature’s bid to win the award for most abhorrent political body in the country, they passed a terrifying $20.5 million immigration package to support Trump’s deportation agenda.
This package FORCES local police departments to do the work of federal immigration offices and puts legal restrictions on how local lawmakers can vote on sanctuary policies, prying away any protections for our local communities.

These Republicans are intent on putting our most vulnerable at risk. It’s a feature, not a bug. They’re brazen and they don’t care if we know it.
---

---
In solidarity,
Ann Perry

name: Kirk Cameron
subject: What is the “Prepare the Way” revival and how can you help?
body:
| | | Brave Books is spearheading a massive "Prepare the Way" revival campaign to shift the focus of Easter from bunnies and chocolate...
---
| |
---
| | Dear Fellow Believer, It may seem a little early to be talking about Easter, but it's really only about 12 weeks away.And in that short amount of time, my friends at Brave Books are spearheading a massive "Prepare the Way" campaign to shift the focus of Easter from bunnies and chocolate......to Jesus.And this revival mission needs you! My friend, if you've seen me talking about Brave Books on Fox News, you know their mission is to counter the ungodly lies being pushed by the Left in schools, libraries, and Hollywood......by creating high-quality, wholesome, and Godly books and entertainment that instill conservative values and Gospel lessons in our children. And their "Prepare the Way" revival campaign is their biggest effort yet to point parents and children to the empty tomb and God’s redeeming love.Here’s exactly what their strategy is...First... Brave Books knows that families need an easy and impactful way to counter the Left's secularization of Easter and instead, captivate children with its true meaning. So, they created _Saving the Easter Bunny_ , a brand-new children's book that's destined to be a classic.In it, Ronnie the Rabbit learns the hard way what sin is and that our Lord Jesus Christ loves us so much that he took the punishment for that sin.Jesus is represented by a powerful lion named Lord Joshua and the book beautifully portrays his resurrection and God's never-ending redeeming love for us. It's incredible.And let me tell you, parents are hungry for content like this because everywhere they turn godlessness is being pushed by schools, left-wing publishers like Scholastic, and Hollywood. When Brave Books first introduced a God-centered Christmas game called "_Mouse in the House_ ," to counter the secular elf game that has become so popular -- it sold out in THREE HOURS!That's why step one of Brave Books' 12-week "Prepare the Way" revival, is ramping up the printing and distribution of _Saving the Easter Bunny_ big-time. **[And today I'm hoping you'll help them kick it into high gear before orders start pouring in by rushing back your best "Prepare the Way" gift.](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=88b4720fc9b24d20aa4373bc4c9236bf&_e=_UtWfppsP6T_4nvZYGrMmso2M68pHVvXo8PULRL1EPsnjnike55brM-RhGzKsb2ioEF4KVZNfGGG_YNqQWA8S9YgfHYKVGpKJopLi9Gc4FAhrKF5LBDPaAwqSiowJoyxnD0CXaqYk55ES_Vmw0SQcMe4Faw8--1--_4asQvnQUG0AGZZjbGuMXMRuDpZ6qsG1Gh1DJKe5TPEA0Fqesj4JO-Kq1RQR42Gmcm7XQx3asMoJk5P9gAEKr6LrZWePkA9j5UZ3_PJmC-Q-qROZs1J7EsQaOtpbEjikxhO53gRnIZmJQpUU3PGhFpZmVzPCzCz6PUg-uPWTot3O3LGr21kcVT-xtVs09_KiaR8tBU7f_R_yUQmKrx0zn8hTAb-qbOTrY_Va14zl17MTYVuOt1E7A%3D%3D)** No family should go without this wonderful book because of overwhelming demand. Second... Recognizing that families who want to raise their children with wholesome Christian values often feel alone in their mission...Brave Books is launching a 17-city traveling church tour that starts in Ponta Vedra Beach, Florida and ends in Laurel, Mississippi. I'll be leading the tour in every city as we prepare our hearts and our families for Easter through prayer, worship, music, and just some good old-fashioned conversation about raising Godly children in our godless culture.Our church tour aims to ignite a spirit of revival in thousands of families this Easter season and I can't wait to see what God makes of that! But getting our worship teams, musicians, and all the rest to 17 different cities for thousands of families to enjoy won't be easy and it won't be inexpensive.But I know we can do it.Brave Books is a small Christian company founded by a doctor named Trent Talbot. After having his first child, he saw how the Left was using books and entertainment to turn the hearts and minds of America's children away from God. And so he decided to take action and with the help of believers just like you, look at what they've already done:
---
>>> They've countered the Left's radical and ungodly "Drag Queen Story Hours" and filled children's hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God with their highly-publicized "See You at the Library" campaign. More than 200 years ago, when our country wasn't even 50 years old and Missouri wasn't yet a state, my ancestors came west and made Missouri their home. A few decades later, just after the civil war, my great great grandpa, Henry Ernest Warren, a captain in the union army, settled in Missouri, married one of their descendants, and opened Missouri's longest running family store in Richland. My family has deep roots in Missouri, going back 8 generations.
My wife, Marilyn, on the other hand, moved to the US from Mexico as a young adult, and then settled with me in Missouri. Yet her family might have even deeper Missouri roots than mine.
Because hundreds or thousands of years before my ancestors settled Missouri, her ancestors roamed the Great Plains and trod this ground before migrating south. How many generations of them lived and died in our state or our country we'll never know.
But we are here together now, and this is how she made it happen, against the odds.

* * *
Dear Neighbors and Friends,
My maiden name is Marilyn Martinez Rivera, and I'm writing to share my story as an immigrant.
To help you better understand where I come from, I want to start with my early life. My dad was a farmer just outside a little town called Guadalupe Victoria in northern Mexico. Alongside my mom, an elementary school teacher, my two siblings, and our pig--funny enough named "Dollar"--we all lived on the farm my dad bought with his life savings.
We were a typical middle- class family. I remember our farm was filled with bunnies, cows, chickens, nut trees, crops, and fruit trees like oranges, apples, and peaches. Baby bunnies, with their tiny ears and soft fur, will forever be my favorite animal (though I must admit, I didn't love them quite as much when they grew big and fat).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c7db29f-ce92-4149-95be-493145d1289c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_On the farm_
One of my favorite memories is of the three pools my dad built on the farm. They weren't fancy or professionally made, but they brought us so much joy. We spent countless hot summer days swimming in the cold water. I wish I could say I ever became a fast swimmer who could beat my siblings in a race, but I didn't spend enough years on that little piece of paradise to get there.
When I was six years old, we had to leave the farm. My dad sold it for little profit--just enough to buy a house closer to town. The farm couldn't grow crops anymore because of the changing climate. Just like here in America, my dad and the other farmers in town face either too much rain at once or long stretches of drought, with intense heat that made it impossible for anything to thrive. Our house was also often struck by lightning, leaving us without power for days. It was a tough decision, but my dad did what he had to do.
On top of that, the country was in an economic recession, and our family was struggling to make ends meet. My dad opened a butcher shop, and on weekends, we ran a small food truck selling hamburgers. My sister got a part-time job at a shoe store, my brother worked at a mechanic shop, and I started singing at festivals and events at age seven to contribute a little money.
This dynamic lasted a few years, but when my brother became old enough for college, our financial situation became even harder. My parents took on debt to send him to school in the nearest city. Both my brother and I were good students and earned scholarships, but these were small--just $20 every two weeks--which we immediately gave to our parents to help with household expenses. I took a part-time job at a boutique, and my mom worked tirelessly to help cover my brother's tuition. Around that time, my sister was diagnosed with diabetes at age 14.
She spent 11 days in the hospital, nearly slipping into a diabetic coma before doctors stabilized her. Our family was truly in financial trouble, but we all contributed, and our friends in the community helped us stay afloat.
You might wonder why my parents prioritized sending my brother to college instead of having him work. The answer is simple: my dad never had the chance to go to school, growing up on the streets since the age of seven, and my mom only had a teaching certificate. From the beginning, they made a pact: if they had kids, those kids would go to college. I am proud to say that my brother not only graduated but went on to earn a Ph.D. in biotechnology, a master's in environmental sciences, and a bachelor's in biochemistry.
My last year of high school was challenging--there were 11 girls in my class, and only three of us weren't pregnant. The other two became mothers the year after graduation, but one still managed to complete her degree and become a lawyer. I'm so proud of her for not giving up on her dreams, especially with a child in her arms.
I took a gap year to save money and afford college myself. I started elementary school ahead of schedule, enrolling in first grade at age four. So, taking a gap year later wasn't a big deal in comparison, but that year served as a huge reminder of my goals and my determination to do more. I had a dream of being part of the change needed in our society to provide opportunities to improve the "calidad de vida" (quality of life) for people.
I worked all through college to pay for it. I held three jobs and never asked my parents for a penny while they were working hard to pay off the debt they had taken on for my brother's education. I don't remember sleeping more than five hours a night during those 4.5 years, but I graduated with honors at the top of my accounting class. I worked as an accountant for a few years, earning just enough to cover basic needs. Life offered two choices: settle for surviving or find a second job to escape the paycheck-to- paycheck lifestyle. I created a third choice.
I signed up for a program to come to America legally to work. My plan was to eventually pursue a master's degree and find an international job that paid a little more. Given the financial struggles my family endured growing up, I was determined to create a life where I had more than just enough to get by. I also wanted to give something back to my family and community one day. So, I took the leap, got myself into debt to get into the program--which was the only way to afford it--and came to the United States to work temporarily and help the kids I was watching learn Spanish.
When I arrived, I had only one $20 bill to my name--just enough to cover the metro card I needed to drop the kids off at school that first week. What I didn't know was that I wouldn't be paid until the end of the week, and it was February, with snow on the ground. I had one light jacket with me and no money for food.
That week, I survived on two mandarins a day, thanks to a bag of cuties I found in the fridge of my basement apartment. I'll never forget how grateful I was for those little fruits. In that moment, I made a promise to myself: I would work tirelessly to ensure I'd never find myself in such a situation again.
During that time, I met another immigrant worker. She was from Costa Rica and she could tell what was going on matter how I tried to hide it. That weekend, when I caught the worst cold of my life--likely from being underdressed for the weather--she quietly left a sandwich, a $20 bill, and one of her old jackets at my door. Her kindness was a lifeline, and Marilu and her husband Luis remain blessings in my life to this day.
During this temporary work period, I applied for permanent jobs in the US. I was a professional accountant in Mexico, but I wanted to pursue the American dream. Which, of course, is how so many immigrants get taken advantage of, whether it's in the tech industry, agriculture, or construction. I must have submitted over 100 resumes, got called for five interviews, and was in the process of landing one offer. However, before I could start, my visa ran out, and I returned to Mexico.
Going back home was bittersweet. It didn't feel like the same home I had left two years earlier, and I wasn't the same person who had left. I had grown, changed, and come closer than ever to achieving my dreams. But just as I was settling back, I received devastating news--I had a tumor in my middle ear and urgently needed open-head surgery.
I spent every penny I had saved and took out another loan to pay for the procedure. The risks were terrifying: I could die during the surgery, lose hearing in that ear, develop irreversible facial paralysis, or need to relearn basic motor skills. But without the surgery, the tumor would reach my brain in what doctors said would be less than a year, and I'd suffer a stroke. Thankfully, none of the worst outcomes came to pass, and I recovered completely.
A couple of months later, I got a job offer as a program assistant at a US non-profit. They needed someone fluent in English and Spanish with a background in Latin America and accounting for an international program reducing the use of mercury in small-scale gold mining. I was so lucky.
It was meaningful work, protecting workers and our worldwide water-supply from the largest source of the global mercury pollution that has contaminated our food supply. I accepted the offer, and after months of navigating the process to obtain a professional worker visa, I moved back to America. I worked tirelessly to pay off my medical debt and grew in my role.
Today, I work as the coordinator of our Latin American Projects, and by the end of spring, I will finish my master's degree in Public Affairs at the University of Missouri. I have a wonderful husband who shares my dream of improving the quality of life for others. Together, we work every day, in small but meaningful ways, to make the world a better place for our children and our communities.
At its core, my journey has been about resilience and determination. While I was fortunate enough to pursue my education and secure a work visa, I know many others aren't as lucky.
Their stories are often even more challenging--seeking safety, opportunity, and a place to belong.
These are values that unite us all, no matter where we come from.
Unfortunately, stories like mine are often overshadowed by harmful stereotypes that misrepresent who we are. Stereotypes created by those who want to take advantage of immigrants and non-immigrants alike. These narratives divide us, and immigrants--particularly Hispanic and Latin people--receive the brunt of it. Even as a legal permanent resident, I sometimes fear for myself or my kids, with whom I intend to share my heritage with. Lately, even that feels unsafe because anyone who looks or sounds like me can become a target.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/23bc43bf-2b3e-4880-b840-70e2018600ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I can only imagine the uncertainty faced by Dreamers--those who were brought here as children, who have no connection to their countries of origin, and who now live in limbo, with some even being asked to leave the only home they've ever known.
We can do better. I invite you to reach out, ask questions, and learn more about the many different journeys that shape our community. Together, we can create a space where everyone feels safe, seen, valued, and respected.
Thank you for taking the time to read my story. It's through understanding and compassion that we can build a stronger, more unified community.
Marilyn Kunce

My family has deep roots in Missouri, going back 8 generations. My wife, Marilyn, on the other hand, moved to the US from Mexico as a young adult, and then settled with me in Missouri. Yet her family might have even deeper Missouri roots than mine. Because hundreds or thousands of years before my ancestors settled Missouri, her ancestors roamed the Great Plains and trod this ground before migrating south. How many generations of them lived and died in our state or our country we'll never know. But we are here together now, and this is how she made it happen, against the odds. Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. * Dear Neighbors and Friends, My maiden name is Marilyn Martinez Rivera, and I'm writing to share my story as an immigrant. To help you better understand where I come from, I want to start with my early life. My dad was a farmer just outside a little town called Guadalupe Victoria in northern Mexico. Alongside my mom, an elementary school teacher, my two siblings, and our pig--funny enough named "Dollar"--we all lived on the farm my dad bought with his life savings. We were a typical middle- class family. I remember our farm was filled with bunnies, cows, chickens, nut trees, crops, and fruit trees like oranges, apples, and peaches. Baby bunnies, with their tiny ears and soft fur, will forever be my favorite animal (though I must admit, I didn't love them quite as much when they grew big and fat). | | ---|---|--- On the farm One of my favorite memories is of the three pools my dad built on the farm. They weren't fancy or professionally made, but they brought us so much joy. We spent countless hot summer days swimming in the cold water. I wish I could say I ever became a fast swimmer who could beat my siblings in a race, but I didn't spend enough years on that little piece of paradise to get there. When I was six years old, we had to leave the farm. My dad sold it for little profit--just enough to buy a house closer to town. The farm couldn't grow crops anymore because of the changing climate. Just like here in America, my dad and the other farmers in town face either too much rain at once or long stretches of drought, with intense heat that made it impossible for anything to thrive. Our house was also often struck by lightning, leaving us without power for days. It was a tough decision, but my dad did what he had to do. On top of that, the country was in an economic recession, and our family was struggling to make ends meet. My dad opened a butcher shop, and on weekends, we ran a small food truck selling hamburgers. My sister got a part-time job at a shoe store, my brother worked at a mechanic shop, and I started singing at festivals and events at age seven to contribute a little money. This dynamic lasted a few years, but when my brother became old enough for college, our financial situation became even harder. My parents took on debt to send him to school in the nearest city. Both my brother and I were good students and earned scholarships, but these were small--just $20 every two weeks--which we immediately gave to our parents to help with household expenses. I took a part-time job at a boutique, and my mom worked tirelessly to help cover my brother's tuition. Around that time, my sister was diagnosed with diabetes at age 14. She spent 11 days in the hospital, nearly slipping into a diabetic coma before doctors stabilized her. Our family was truly in financial trouble, but we all contributed, and our friends in the community helped us stay afloat. You might wonder why my parents prioritized sending my brother to college instead of having him work. The answer is simple: my dad never had the chance to go to school, growing up on the streets since the age of seven, and my mom only had a teaching certificate. From the beginning, they made a pact: if they had kids, those kids would go to college. I am proud to say that my brother not only graduated but went on to earn a Ph.D. in biotechnology, a master's in environmental sciences, and a bachelor's in biochemistry. My last year of high school was challenging--there were 11 girls in my class, and only three of us weren't pregnant. The other two became mothers the year after graduation, but one still managed to complete her degree and become a lawyer. I'm so proud of her for not giving up on her dreams, especially with a child in her arms. I took a gap year to save money and afford college myself. I started elementary school ahead of schedule, enrolling in first grade at age four. So, taking a gap year later wasn't a big deal in comparison, but that year served as a huge reminder of my goals and my determination to do more. I had a dream of being part of the change needed in our society to provide opportunities to improve the "calidad de vida" (quality of life) for people. I worked all through college to pay for it. I held three jobs and never asked my parents for a penny while they were working hard to pay off the debt they had taken on for my brother's education. I don't remember sleeping more than five hours a night during those 4.5 years, but I graduated with honors at the top of my accounting class. I worked as an accountant for a few years, earning just enough to cover basic needs. Life offered two choices: settle for surviving or find a second job to escape the paycheck-to- paycheck lifestyle. I created a third choice. I signed up for a program to come to America legally to work. My plan was to eventually pursue a master's degree and find an international job that paid a little more. Given the financial struggles my family endured growing up, I was determined to create a life where I had more than just enough to get by. I also wanted to give something back to my family and community one day. So, I took the leap, got myself into debt to get into the program--which was the only way to afford it--and came to the United States to work temporarily and help the kids I was watching learn Spanish. When I arrived, I had only one $20 bill to my name--just enough to cover the metro card I needed to drop the kids off at school that first week. What I didn't know was that I wouldn't be paid until the end of the week, and it was February, with snow on the ground. I had one light jacket with me and no money for food. That week, I survived on two mandarins a day, thanks to a bag of cuties I found in the fridge of my basement apartment. I'll never forget how grateful I was for those little fruits. In that moment, I made a promise to myself: I would work tirelessly to ensure I'd never find myself in such a situation again. During that time, I met another immigrant worker. She was from Costa Rica and she could tell what was going on matter how I tried to hide it. That weekend, when I caught the worst cold of my life--likely from being underdressed for the weather--she quietly left a sandwich, a $20 bill, and one of her old jackets at my door. Her kindness was a lifeline, and Marilu and her husband Luis remain blessings in my life to this day. During this temporary work period, I applied for permanent jobs in the US. I was a professional accountant in Mexico, but I wanted to pursue the American dream. Which, of course, is how so many immigrants get taken advantage of, whether it's in the tech industry, agriculture, or construction. I must have submitted over 100 resumes, got called for five interviews, and was in the process of landing one offer. However, before I could start, my visa ran out, and I returned to Mexico. Going back home was bittersweet. It didn't feel like the same home I had left two years earlier, and I wasn't the same person who had left. I had grown, changed, and come closer than ever to achieving my dreams. But just as I was settling back, I received devastating news--I had a tumor in my middle ear and urgently needed open-head surgery. I spent every penny I had saved and took out another loan to pay for the procedure. The risks were terrifying: I could die during the surgery, lose hearing in that ear, develop irreversible facial paralysis, or need to relearn basic motor skills. But without the surgery, the tumor would reach my brain in what doctors said would be less than a year, and I'd suffer a stroke. Thankfully, none of the worst outcomes came to pass, and I recovered completely. A couple of months later, I got a job offer as a program assistant at a US non-profit. They needed someone fluent in English and Spanish with a background in Latin America and accounting for an international program reducing the use of mercury in small-scale gold mining. I was so lucky. It was meaningful work, protecting workers and our worldwide water-supply from the largest source of the global mercury pollution that has contaminated our food supply. I accepted the offer, and after months of navigating the process to obtain a professional worker visa, I moved back to America. I worked tirelessly to pay off my medical debt and grew in my role. Today, I work as the coordinator of our Latin American Projects, and by the end of spring, I will finish my master's degree in Public Affairs at the University of Missouri. I have a wonderful husband who shares my dream of improving the quality of life for others. Together, we work every day, in small but meaningful ways, to make the world a better place for our children and our communities. At its core, my journey has been about resilience and determination. While I was fortunate enough to pursue my education and secure a work visa, I know many others aren't as lucky. Their stories are often even more challenging--seeking safety, opportunity, and a place to belong. These are values that unite us all, no matter where we come from. Unfortunately, stories like mine are often overshadowed by harmful stereotypes that misrepresent who we are. Stereotypes created by those who want to take advantage of immigrants and non-immigrants alike. These narratives divide us, and immigrants--particularly Hispanic and Latin people--receive the brunt of it. Even as a legal permanent resident, I sometimes fear for myself or my kids, with whom I intend to share my heritage with. Lately, even that feels unsafe because anyone who looks or sounds like me can become a target. | | ---|---|--- I can only imagine the uncertainty faced by Dreamers--those who were brought here as children, who have no connection to their countries of origin, and who now live in limbo, with some even being asked to leave the only home they've ever known. We can do better. I invite you to reach out, ask questions, and learn more about the many different journeys that shape our community. Together, we can create a space where everyone feels safe, seen, valued, and respected. Thank you for taking the time to read my story. It's through understanding and compassion that we can build a stronger, more unified community. Marilyn Kunce Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. body:
The confusion and chaos is part of the strategy.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=39414%2E3422442%2Eq4gLSd)
Derek, it’s Katie Porter.
I filmed a video about Trump’s order to freeze spending on federal loans and grants yesterday morning...
By the time I could post it yesterday between teaching classes, the Trump Administration rescinded guidance given to federal agencies about the freeze. But the freeze itself is still in effect.
The confusion and chaos is part of the strategy. Don't lose sight of what's under attack: freezing federal spending will harm kids who can’t get school lunch, seniors who see programs disappear, and entire communities that can’t get disaster relief.
I broke down the confusing BS from the Trump admin yesterday, **[if you have two minutes, you can watch my video on that here.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20250130?refcode=em20250130-39414&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39414_3422442_q4gLSd&akid=39414%2E3422442%2Eq4gLSd)**

Republicans talk a _big game_ about being the party of freedom – but Peter, I don’t buy it:

➡ Democrats are the ones fighting for the freedom to make **your own choices with your body,** while Republicans push bills to ban access to contraceptives.

➡ Democrats are the ones fighting for the freedom to **afford healthcare, housing, and childcare,** while Republicans try to make these _harder_ to access.

➡ Democrats are the ones fighting for the **freedom to love who you want, and be who you want, without fear,** while Republicans roll back progress for the LGBTQ+ community.

The mantra of the vote suppressors must be "if you can't beat 'em," Team, "just try and get their votes thrown out".
This may be happening in North Carolina but it's a problem everywhere. As Republican Justice Richard Dietz said in his scathing dissent, joining his lone Democratic colleague: “ the timing of Griffin’s claims speaks volumes about their substance. By waiting until after the votes were cast and the results tallied, Griffin seeks to retroactively rewrite the rules of the election to tilt the playing field in his favor .”
In other words: The challenger's campaign only sued to get these votes tossed because he lost.
This isn't about false claims of "election integrity" or whatever buzzwords opponents of voting rights use, this is blatant retroactive voter suppression. RUSH $25 or more today to stop vengeful partisans from wrongfully silencing these voters, flipping this election, and more >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=013025_3&amount=25]

NC Newsline: Republicans on the NC Supreme Court block certification of the Democratic incumbent’s election [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=013025_3&amount=25]
This case is still going on in North Carolina, Team, and we have to spread the word because the media is ignoring election theft in plain sight.
The North Carolina state Supreme Court stepped in to stop the certification of the election for a justice on their court , which is a huge breach of power and a clearly partisan action in a state where judges are affiliated with political parties.
For background: On Election Day, incumbent Justice Allison Riggs (D) was reelected by a slim margin of a few hundred votes. Her disgruntled opponent, GOP Judge Jefferson Griffin, sued for and received two separate recounts -- both of which increased Riggs' lead.
Now Judge Griffin has sued to remove 60,000 voters' ballots from the count , even though they've been validated in the recount. The state Board of Elections dismissed his request , but now his partisan, would-be colleagues -- the court has a 5-2 Republican majority -- have stepped in to adjudicate the election and possibly kick off one of their own.
Justices Anita Earls (D) and Richard Dietz (R) dissented while Justice Riggs properly recused herself, so the judicial stay on election certification was put in place by a 4-2, mainly party-line vote.
The bottom line is that the partisan Supreme Court is stepping into an election for one of their own members to try and reverse the results of the vote because their party didn't win. Opponents of voting rights are trying to steal this election in plain sight.
We've got to make sure everyone knows about this egregious intervention before these votes are stolen and the voices of the people are silenced. And shortly after I started a career in property management, I ran for public office. _Why?_ Because like you, I'm a pro-life conservative who's sick of seeing God's unborn children being killed, mutilated, and harvested... I'm sick of seeing obesity and opioids decimate our communities and ruin the lives of an entire generation of Americans - _perhaps your children or grandchildren..._ And I'm sick of seeing citizens like you and me lied to by our own government and told that we can never question their authority. They're "debating" whether to confirm President Trump's nominations, or if the American people will let them get away with installing their Swamp buddies instead. And they're "debating" how much money should go to the war machine in Ukraine, instead of using those tax dollars to build the wall, bring manufacturing jobs back to America, and invest in safer streets and stronger families. Now, Republicans like you and me have some real fighters in the House... body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Donald Trump’s anti-immigrant and Islamophobic agenda is already ramping
up in his first week back in office.

On Monday, the far-right president signed an executive order paving the
way for a new, worse Muslim ban.

[2]Al Jazeera: Trump decree paves way for 'Muslim ban', targeting
pro-Palestine students

If implemented, this order would not only ban people from several
Muslim-majority nations from entering the U.S. like the first time around,
but it would revoke visas and deport students and other immigrants who
participated in anti-war protests in support of peace in Palestine. It’s a
direct attack on freedom of speech.

[3]A screenshot of a post on X from @IfNotNowOrg: We are disgusted that
Trump & his antisemitic, neo-Nazi allies are planning to deport students &
other immigrants for protesting the Israeli military's assult on Gaza,
while gutting academic freedom by threatening to withhold billions in
federal funding from universities.

And yesterday, Trump announced plans to use the Guantanamo Bay detention
center to indefinitely detain tens of thousands of migrants.[4]A
screenshot of a post on X from Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez. She is
quoting a video of President Trump speaking with the caption 'Today I'm
also signing an executive order to instruct the Department of Defense and
Homeland Security to begin preparing the 30,000 person migrant facility at
Guantanamo Bay. Most people don't even know about it.' Congresswoman
Ramirez replied with 'Guantanamo hosted some of our most shameful acts of
violence, dehumanization, and humiliation. It should be closed and the
land returned to Cuba. No repurposed. Not expanded. And definitely not
turned into a detention camp for immigrants. (1/2)'

These are despicable attacks targeted at immigrant and Muslim communities,
but once again, Justice Democrats and the Squad will fight back just like
we did the first time around.

We’re not just resisting—we’re fighting back. Together, we will challenge
and speak out against this fascist administration’s racism, xenophobia,
and Islamophobia and our progressive incumbents are leading the fight to
protect these targeted communities in their districts.

These attacks are meant to divide our communities against each other, but
we know better. We know that our struggles are interconnected, an attack
on one of us is an attack on all of us, and only by uniting our
communities together can we build the movement that will defeat this
billionaire-backed right-wing extremism.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. In the summer of 1990, Raul walked in the desert heat from business to business in the Coachella Valley asking them to invest in their community by contributing to his education. With each investment for college, he made a promise to come back home and serve his community as a physician. In 2012, he decided to take his service to the community to the next level by running for Congress. **Dr. Ruiz needs our help to continue fighting for us in Congress.**

I just finished up an appearance on MSNBC, where I talked with Lawrence O’Donnell about Tulsi Gabbard’s hearing in the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and explained why I'm voting against her confirmation.

We discussed my concerns about her experience and qualifications, ability to build and develop trusting relationships with our allies, and her tendency to excuse our adversaries for their worst actions and instead blame them on the U.S. We also spoke about Gabbard’s responses to my concerns and those of my colleagues.

Today’s hearing was an important one, and I’m glad I was able to directly address Gabbard about her past.

Remember, Derek, I am always looking out for you in the Senate. If Gabbard, or frankly, any of Trump’s other nominees, don’t have the know-how or the judgment to do these jobs, I will get to the bottom of it.

Thank you,

Mark Warner

name: Hillsdale College via Updates For Great Americans
subject: Who rules whom?
body:
The Constitution of “We the People” is being replaced by an elite, out-of-touch, and unaccountable administrative state that rules without the consent of American citizens.

This sponsored message from Great America Update is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | |
---
| | [](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2z0th48j7t3p2b03nnqdpdlekkm83lnbgoah75sbg_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph68oj3cjh2bs)
---
| | | Dear Fellow American, Hillsdale College has selected you to participate in its [**National Referendum on the Administrative State**](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2z5ah83elltdp3kcdefdstkbc9qt9s83chbtogkh8_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph68oj3cjh2bs).

Responding will only take a few minutes. Your input as an informed patriot is needed right away...because **our country is facing a constitutional crisis**.

It's a crisis that involves a fundamental political question: **who rules whom?**

The Constitution established a limited government in which the **people** ruled through their elected officials. Under this form of government, America became the freest and most prosperous nation in history.

Today, however, our constitutional system is one that increasingly exists in name only. **The Constitution of "We the People" is being replaced by an elite, out-of-touch, and unaccountable administrative state that rules without the consent of American citizens.** This means we live in an era of growing bureaucratic despotism, manifested in an administrative state that bypasses the Constitution, rejects the separation of powers, and replaces the rule of law with regulations.

**But we can 't just TALK about the problem. We also have to TAKE ACTION--to DO SOMETHING about it, while there's still time to save our country. **

That is why I'm writing to you today.

Hillsdale College is committed to returning to the Constitution of "We the People"--before it's too late.

To do that, I need your input. What are your opinions on this topic--knowing that we can propose SOLUTIONS that will restore liberty?

**Please let me know your thoughts today by answering the National Referendum on the Administrative State using this secure link:**

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/administrative-state-survey](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2ziahivvobv340hch5isc06ihm8s1ufa650ouh0ag_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph68oj3cjh2bs)**

When you send in your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

The rise of the administrative state is a grave threat to our country.

To counter this threat, Hillsdale sponsors several educational outreach efforts--including _Imprimis_ , free online courses, programs on our Washington, D.C., campus, and a growing network of classical K-12 schools and homeschoolers--to teach citizens about the meaning of the Constitution and the importance of our founding principles of liberty.

Your gift of at least $15--or even $25, $35, $50, $100, or more if you're especially motivated to TAKE ACTION--will help us to expand these educational initiatives that are reaching and teaching millions.

Your support of these efforts is essential because Hillsdale refuses to take ONE PENNY of government funding.

So please complete your **National Referendum on the Administrative State** and consider giving your most generous tax-deductible contribution.

Thank you for being on the side of the Constitution and liberty!

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn
President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

**P.S.** I look forward to receiving your opinions about what's happening in our nation. And I hope that you can support our work.

So please complete the **National Referendum on the Administrative State** using this secure link:

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/administrative-state-survey](https://e.updatesforgreatamericans.com/rd/9z2z4rvtbl6ol1n14ctt6vts5jdvlpnrepmp82c2oog_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph68oj3cjh2bs)**

As soon as you respond, we will begin your FREE lifetime subscription to _Imprimis_ , Hillsdale's digest of liberty that you will receive via email ten times a year. If you'd like, you can also sign up to receive the publication through postal mail.

Educating millions about the Constitution to counter the threat from the administrative state is a monumental task. That's why when you complete your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Thank you for your time and attention--and for your commitment to liberty.
---
| | Hillsdale College 33 East College St Hillsdale, MI 49242 USA

body:
In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift among young Americans who increasingly favor socialism over capitalism.

| | | [](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zeln0ssrd4du70occ04f986uahju5i7q7n6dcd80_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph68oj5cdh2bs)

---

| | To address this, we have created a new eBook, _**The History of Socialism and Capitalism**_ , authored by two of the most prominent voices in today's political discourse, Hoover Institution senior fellows Niall Ferguson and Victor Davis Hanson.

This new eBook offers a deep dive into the origins, development, and impacts of socialism and capitalism. Each scholar presents an in-depth analysis through two different lenses. It's hard to overstate the relevance of this eBook in today's policy debates, where radical proposals are gaining traction.

Understanding the historical and practical implications of socialism and capitalism is crucial for making informed decisions about our economic and political future. The insights provided by Ferguson and Hanson will equip you with the knowledge to critically evaluate these competing ideologies and their potential impact on society.

body:
what a month

Friend, let's recap January...

✅ _President Trump is back in the White House_

✅ _Republicans are back in control of the Senate_

✅ _We added TWO new Republican Senators, Ashley Moody in Florida and Jon Husted in Ohio_

✅ _Senate Republicans are working around the clock to break through the Democrats ' blockade, confirm President Trump's team, and put America First_

## Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

body:
In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift among young Americans who increasingly favor socialism over capitalism.

| | | [](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zlh4o4vo7onj1mrtsmjmp4pdbaccftarilqc4g5o_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph6co36cdh2bs)
---
| | Dear Friend, In recent years, there has been a noticeable shift among young Americans who increasingly favor socialism over capitalism. This trend raises a critical question: do they fully understand these two systems' historical contexts and real-world outcomes?
---
| [](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zodkm0o3dde4piv4uejesede97j0vnt2rt9jns20_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph6co36cdh2bs)
---
| | To address this, we have created a new eBook, _**The History of Socialism and Capitalism**_ , authored by two of the most prominent voices in today's political discourse, Hoover Institution senior fellows Niall Ferguson and Victor Davis Hanson.

This new eBook offers a deep dive into the origins, development, and impacts of socialism and capitalism. Each scholar presents an in-depth analysis through two different lenses. It's hard to overstate the relevance of this eBook in today's policy debates, where radical proposals are gaining traction.

Understanding the historical and practical implications of socialism and capitalism is crucial for making informed decisions about our economic and political future. The insights provided by Ferguson and Hanson will equip you with the knowledge to critically evaluate these competing ideologies and their potential impact on society.

Don't miss this opportunity to enhance your understanding of these pivotal economic systems. [Click here to request your free copy of **The History of Socialism and Capitalism** today.](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zf531tu6um67692239bjtug664qplknj03k86sng_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph6co36cdh2bs)

name: Lacy Lunsford
subject: We’re running out of time
body:
Our nightmare started the day my husband responded to a shoplifting call.

| | | my husband had no choice -- it was the suspect’s life or his partner’s.
---
| |
---
Dear Friend,My husband saved the life of his fellow officer and now, on February 3rd, a Soros-funded prosecutor is going to try and lock him up for _11 years_.
Here is one of my favorite pictures of our two boys.
---
[](https://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zume9dlu6bqa6nej8rubgp5hhpdamkma6b5cq03g_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph62o75cth2bs)
---
[](https://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2znro257bl4lhc20p1eo0iintf4bt5tqqf0sn3vs8_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph62o75cth2bs)
---
Now it makes me cry. As you can probably tell from my sons' costumes, my husband Brad is a proud U.S. Army veteran. He served two tours of duty in Iraq as a Cavalry Scout. And today he is also a decorated, 9-year veteran of the Las Cruces, New Mexico, police department. I'm used to my husband being in danger. But never in my wildest dreams did I think the biggest threat to Brad wouldn't come from a radical terrorist or a violent gangster... ...but from a _Soros-funded_ , _anti-police_ _prosecutor_. **[**That's why I'm writing you today as a last resort to ask if you'll help me fight for my husband.**](https://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zkv3fnbamgglr8pnj535ad3p5rsonho7kn9bb278_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph62o75cth2bs)** Our nightmare started the day my husband responded to a shoplifting call. When Brad arrived on the scene, right away he sensed something was off. And when he and his partner, Officer Keegan Arbogast, asked the suspect to identify himself, the suspect refused. So when Officer Arbogast saw a knife sitting on the suspect's lap, hidden under a water bottle, the officers moved to detain him. Instead of complying, the suspect got violent. Everything that happened next happened in an instant. As the officers tried to subdue him, the suspect went for Officer Arbogast's gun, trying to pull it from the holster. Then he lunged for Officer Arbogast's taser, yanked it free, and pointed it directly at him. In that moment, my husband had no choice -- it was the suspect's life or his partner's. He drew his pistol and fired, killing the suspect and saving Officer Arbogast's life. When one of Brad's coworkers called me to tell me there had been a shooting, I burst into tears. I didn't stop crying until Brad came home. I was so thankful he was safe. I knew he did what he had to do to protect his partner so they could both make it home to their families. And when an Internal Investigation _and_ the local District Attorney cleared my husband of any wrongdoing, I thought this awful episode was behind us. I couldn't have been more wrong. Because more than a year after the incident, the Attorney General of New Mexico charged my husband with Voluntary Manslaughter! When I heard about the charges, I was shocked. Then we did some digging -- and it all made sense. The New Mexico Attorney General is a rabid far-Left activist who _hates_ the police. He was funded by George Soros. And because my husband is white, and the suspect was black... ...this radical prosecutor is determined to make a name for himself by destroying my husband and dragging his name through the mud. He even held a press conference and turned the microphone over to the suspect's family so they could spread hateful lies about my husband, smearing him as a "racist" and a "cold-blooded killer." **Make no mistake -- these charges are a slap in the face to every brave man and woman who has ever put on the badge.** Now you can see why I'm so heartbroken and furious. My husband is an honorable man who wanted nothing more than to serve his country and his community. That's why he served for 3 years in the Army as a cavalry scout. And it's why he served for 10 years as a police officer. But more than that, he's a wonderful husband and an incredible father to our 9- and 6-year-old boys. We've tried to explain to our boys as best we can about what's going on. But they're too young to fully understand. And I can't bear to think of what it will do to them if one day, Daddy is taken away and they're forced to grow up with their father behind bars. But unless people like you speak up to defend my husband against these disgusting Soros-funded political attacks... ...Brad will miss 11 years of birthdays, wedding anniversaries, and Little League games. As I mentioned earlier, Brad's trial starts in just days and already, the legal bills have become overwhelming for our family. Thank God, we got a call from Jason Johnson. Jason is a retired police officer -- and he's the President of the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). If you've ever heard of LELDF, you know they're a national group fighting on behalf of wrongly-accused police officers like Brad. LELDF has helped dozens of innocent officers -- and their families -- when it seemed like there was no hope left. And with the thought of losing my husband and trying to suddenly raise my two boys on my own -- I was certainly hopeless. Not only did LELDF decide to help my husband get the legal defense he deserves, they're also raising money to pay for the best lawyers and expert witnesses available. But it’s only because of the support of brave patriots like yourself. Jason and LELDF were an answer to prayer for our family. That's because Brad and I aren't wealthy people. I run our family farm and Brad is a veteran turned cop. So I must ask you one of the toughest questions I've ever asked anyone. **[**Will you donate $35 or any amount to LELDF to help me save my husband?**](https://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zg72ln9mh5u03tvogl4dov5706d4107mp8o4t688_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph62o75cth2bs)** If I had anywhere else to turn, I wouldn't be so bold as to ask for your help. But I'm so scared for Brad and I will do whatever I can for him -- and for our sons. **[So I pray you'll find it in your heart today to make a tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, $100 or more to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund.](https://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zadq0gvp52j1osprf6cbfpss0pohmalh6s0g4na0_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph62o75cth2bs) ** Brad and I -- and our two sons -- are counting on the good nature and generosity of kind neighbors like you to help keep Brad home where he belongs. No matter what you're able to give today, please pray for us. Thank you in advance for your support.
---
Sincerely,
---
Lacy Lunsford
---
| | P.S. I already spent a year apart from my husband when he was in the Army. It's the hardest thing I've ever done. He almost died during that deployment when the Humvee he was driving hit an IED. I can't imagine having to spend 11 long, lonely years, trying to raise the boys by myself -- and worrying every day about my husband, locked up with hundreds of violent criminals. Please don't let my two boys grow up without their father -- [**please follow this link right now to make a tax-deductible donation of $35 or any amount to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund today.**](https://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zf8cutu1dr4jq0okns0s8m5m1n7khqu9u403vnhg_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph62o75cth2bs) P.P.S. Brad's trial starts on February 3rd, so we're quickly running out time. Thank you for helping my family fight back against this Soros-funded prosecutor!
---

He served two tours of duty in Iraq as a Cavalry Scout. And today he is also a decorated, 9-year veteran of the Las Cruces, New Mexico, police department. I'm used to my husband being in danger. But never in my wildest dreams did I think the biggest threat to Brad wouldn't come from a radical terrorist or a violent gangster... ...but from a Soros-funded , anti-police prosecutor. Our nightmare started the day my husband responded to a shoplifting call. When Brad arrived on the scene, right away he sensed something was off. And when he and his partner, Officer Keegan Arbogast, asked the suspect to identify himself, the suspect refused. So when Officer Arbogast saw a knife sitting on the suspect's lap, hidden under a water bottle, the officers moved to detain him. Instead of complying, the suspect got violent. Everything that happened next happened in an instant. As the officers tried to subdue him, the suspect went for Officer Arbogast's gun, trying to pull it from the holster. Then he lunged for Officer Arbogast's taser, yanked it free, and pointed it directly at him. In that moment, my husband had no choice -- it was the suspect's life or his partner's. He drew his pistol and fired, killing the suspect and saving Officer Arbogast's life. When one of Brad's coworkers called me to tell me there had been a shooting, I burst into tears. I didn't stop crying until Brad came home. I was so thankful he was safe. I knew he did what he had to do to protect his partner so they could both make it home to their families. And when an Internal Investigation and the local District Attorney cleared my husband of any wrongdoing, I thought this awful episode was behind us. I couldn't have been more wrong. Because more than a year after the incident, the Attorney General of New Mexico charged my husband with Voluntary Manslaughter! When I heard about the charges, I was shocked. Then we did some digging -- and it all made sense. The New Mexico Attorney General is a rabid far-Left activist who hates the police. He was funded by George Soros. And because my husband is white, and the suspect was black... ...this radical prosecutor is determined to make a name for himself by destroying my husband and dragging his name through the mud. He even held a press conference and turned the microphone over to the suspect's family so they could spread hateful lies about my husband, smearing him as a "racist" and a "cold-blooded killer." Make no mistake -- these charges are a slap in the face to every brave man and woman who has ever put on the badge. Now you can see why I'm so heartbroken and furious. My husband is an honorable man who wanted nothing more than to serve his country and his community. That's why he served for 3 years in the Army as a cavalry scout. And it's why he served for 10 years as a police officer. But more than that, he's a wonderful husband and an incredible father to our 9- and 6-year-old boys. We've tried to explain to our boys as best we can about what's going on. But they're too young to fully understand. And I can't bear to think of what it will do to them if one day, Daddy is taken away and they're forced to grow up with their father behind bars. But unless people like you speak up to defend my husband against these disgusting Soros-funded political attacks... ...Brad will miss 11 years of birthdays, wedding anniversaries, and Little League games. As I mentioned earlier, Brad's trial starts in just days and already, the legal bills have become overwhelming for our family. Thank God, we got a call from Jason Johnson. Jason is a retired police officer -- and he's the President of the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). If you've ever heard of LELDF, you know they're a national group fighting on behalf of wrongly-accused police officers like Brad. LELDF has helped dozens of innocent officers -- and their families -- when it seemed like there was no hope left. And with the thought of losing my husband and trying to suddenly raise my two boys on my own -- I was certainly hopeless. Not only did LELDF decide to help my husband get the legal defense he deserves, they're also raising money to pay for the best lawyers and expert witnesses available. But it’s only because of the support of brave patriots like yourself. Jason and LELDF were an answer to prayer for our family. That's because Brad and I aren't wealthy people. I run our family farm and Brad is a veteran turned cop. So I must ask you one of the toughest questions I've ever asked anyone. If I had anywhere else to turn, I wouldn't be so bold as to ask for your help. But I'm so scared for Brad and I will do whatever I can for him -- and for our sons. Brad and I -- and our two sons -- are counting on the good nature and generosity of kind neighbors like you to help keep Brad home where he belongs. No matter what you're able to give today, please pray for us. Thank you in advance for your support. Sincerely, Lacy Lunsford | | P.S. I can't imagine having to spend 11 long, lonely years, trying to raise the boys by myself -- and worrying every day about my husband, locked up with hundreds of violent criminals. Please don't let my two boys grow up without their father -- P.P.S. Brad's trial starts on February 3rd, so we're quickly running out time. ## Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?
[YES](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zoaeicf8j1bd9clafuf67iacrhk732tgb297k588_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph61ob6c3h2bs) [NO](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2z4k5k14gb7f4tqstpnv8vs17q9obt42d3hubu36o_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph61ob6c3h2bs) Dear Fellow American, I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter. It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future. A movement is growing, led by progressives--but supported by many well-meaning Americans--to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution. That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a **National Survey on Presidential Selection.** By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue--views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders. name: Hillsdale College via American Briefing
subject: Who rules whom?
body:
The Constitution of “We the People” is being replaced by an elite, out-of-touch, and unaccountable administrative state that rules without the consent of American citizens.

This sponsored message from American Briefing is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | |
---
| | [](http://e.americanbriefing.com/rd/9z2zm45oj8hnnak92ajfnb0piaqdh222oc2psbst590_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph69pj0c3h2bs)
---
| | | Dear Fellow American, Hillsdale College has selected you to participate in its [**National Referendum on the Administrative State**](http://e.americanbriefing.com/rd/9z2z9jc04n7btuatahomcumk0t0if61nuqf0cg7v3v0_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph69pj0c3h2bs).

Responding will only take a few minutes. Your input as an informed patriot is needed right away...because **our country is facing a constitutional crisis**.

It's a crisis that involves a fundamental political question: **who rules whom?**

The Constitution established a limited government in which the **people** ruled through their elected officials. Under this form of government, America became the freest and most prosperous nation in history.

Today, however, our constitutional system is one that increasingly exists in name only. **The Constitution of "We the People" is being replaced by an elite, out-of-touch, and unaccountable administrative state that rules without the consent of American citizens.** This means we live in an era of growing bureaucratic despotism, manifested in an administrative state that bypasses the Constitution, rejects the separation of powers, and replaces the rule of law with regulations.

**But we can 't just TALK about the problem. We also have to TAKE ACTION--to DO SOMETHING about it, while there's still time to save our country. **

That is why I'm writing to you today.

Hillsdale College is committed to returning to the Constitution of "We the People"--before it's too late.

To do that, I need your input. What are your opinions on this topic--knowing that we can propose SOLUTIONS that will restore liberty?

**Please let me know your thoughts today by answering the National Referendum on the Administrative State using this secure link:**

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/administrative-state-survey](http://e.americanbriefing.com/rd/9z2zlebd2qr4q3cud6k393l9vpj36br9a464ga9g610_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph69pj0c3h2bs)**

When you send in your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

The rise of the administrative state is a grave threat to our country.

To counter this threat, Hillsdale sponsors several educational outreach efforts--including _Imprimis_ , free online courses, programs on our Washington, D.C., campus, and a growing network of classical K-12 schools and homeschoolers--to teach citizens about the meaning of the Constitution and the importance of our founding principles of liberty.

Your gift of at least $15--or even $25, $35, $50, $100, or more if you're especially motivated to TAKE ACTION--will help us to expand these educational initiatives that are reaching and teaching millions.

Your support of these efforts is essential because Hillsdale refuses to take ONE PENNY of government funding.

So please complete your **National Referendum on the Administrative State** and consider giving your most generous tax-deductible contribution.

Thank you for being on the side of the Constitution and liberty!

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn
President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

**P.S.** I look forward to receiving your opinions about what's happening in our nation. And I hope that you can support our work.

So please complete the **National Referendum on the Administrative State** using this secure link:

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/administrative-state-survey](http://e.americanbriefing.com/rd/9z2z15adavc0q42sr8dvemil2okvv2irtaed69s4dno_rp22sh2s8i6epj0sph69pj0c3h2bs)**

As soon as you respond, we will begin your FREE lifetime subscription to _Imprimis_ , Hillsdale's digest of liberty that you will receive via email ten times a year. If you'd like, you can also sign up to receive the publication through postal mail.

Educating millions about the Constitution to counter the threat from the administrative state is a monumental task. That's why when you complete your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Thank you for your time and attention--and for your commitment to liberty.
---
| | Hillsdale College 33 East College St Hillsdale, MI 49242 USA

It's a fact that Massachusetts has already spent more than $1,000,000,000 of taxpayer money on the migrant crisis, with no real end in sight.
It's a fact multiple MS-13 gang members, murder and rape suspects, and a Haitian gang member with 18 prior convictions, were all arrested in Boston this month.
Rewatching the video, I realized that Mayor Wu was all over the place, saying - "We will continue to follow the law" but "We don't enforce federal immigration law" ? Then Mayor Wu contradicts herself again - "When someone breaks the law here, we hold them accountable, regardless of their immigration status." ?!
This is a clear reminder that Mayor Wu is out to make "Massachusetts into a bold laboratory for progressive state initiatives."

Now it makes me cry. As you can probably tell from my sons' costumes, my husband Brad is a proud U.S. Army veteran. He served two tours of duty in Iraq as a Cavalry Scout. And today he is also a decorated, 9-year veteran of the Las Cruces, New Mexico, police department. I'm used to my husband being in danger. But never in my wildest dreams did I think the biggest threat to Brad wouldn't come from a radical terrorist or a violent gangster... ...but from a _Soros-funded_ , _anti-police_ _prosecutor_. **[**That's why I'm writing you today as a last resort to ask if you'll help me fight for my husband.**](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z4980qlhhtn043gh4a0eib1pbg9t9u7npk7qf5t0_rp22sh2s8i6epj0spj60oj0clh2bs)** Our nightmare started the day my husband responded to a shoplifting call. When Brad arrived on the scene, right away he sensed something was off. And when he and his partner, Officer Keegan Arbogast, asked the suspect to identify himself, the suspect refused. So when Officer Arbogast saw a knife sitting on the suspect's lap, hidden under a water bottle, the officers moved to detain him. Instead of complying, the suspect got violent. Everything that happened next happened in an instant. As the officers tried to subdue him, the suspect went for Officer Arbogast's gun, trying to pull it from the holster. Then he lunged for Officer Arbogast's taser, yanked it free, and pointed it directly at him. In that moment, my husband had no choice -- it was the suspect's life or his partner's. He drew his pistol and fired, killing the suspect and saving Officer Arbogast's life. When one of Brad's coworkers called me to tell me there had been a shooting, I burst into tears. I didn't stop crying until Brad came home. I was so thankful he was safe. I knew he did what he had to do to protect his partner so they could both make it home to their families. And when an Internal Investigation _and_ the local District Attorney cleared my husband of any wrongdoing, I thought this awful episode was behind us. I couldn't have been more wrong. Because more than a year after the incident, the Attorney General of New Mexico charged my husband with Voluntary Manslaughter! When I heard about the charges, I was shocked. Then we did some digging -- and it all made sense. The New Mexico Attorney General is a rabid far-Left activist who _hates_ the police. He was funded by George Soros. And because my husband is white, and the suspect was black... ...this radical prosecutor is determined to make a name for himself by destroying my husband and dragging his name through the mud. He even held a press conference and turned the microphone over to the suspect's family so they could spread hateful lies about my husband, smearing him as a "racist" and a "cold-blooded killer." **Make no mistake -- these charges are a slap in the face to every brave man and woman who has ever put on the badge.** Now you can see why I'm so heartbroken and furious. My husband is an honorable man who wanted nothing more than to serve his country and his community. That's why he served for 3 years in the Army as a cavalry scout. And it's why he served for 10 years as a police officer. But more than that, he's a wonderful husband and an incredible father to our 9- and 6-year-old boys. We've tried to explain to our boys as best we can about what's going on. But they're too young to fully understand. And I can't bear to think of what it will do to them if one day, Daddy is taken away and they're forced to grow up with their father behind bars. But unless people like you speak up to defend my husband against these disgusting Soros-funded political attacks... ...Brad will miss 11 years of birthdays, wedding anniversaries, and Little League games. As I mentioned earlier, Brad's trial starts in just days and already, the legal bills have become overwhelming for our family. Thank God, we got a call from Jason Johnson. Jason is a retired police officer -- and he's the President of the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF). If you've ever heard of LELDF, you know they're a national group fighting on behalf of wrongly-accused police officers like Brad. LELDF has helped dozens of innocent officers -- and their families -- when it seemed like there was no hope left. And with the thought of losing my husband and trying to suddenly raise my two boys on my own -- I was certainly hopeless. Not only did LELDF decide to help my husband get the legal defense he deserves, they're also raising money to pay for the best lawyers and expert witnesses available. But it’s only because of the support of brave patriots like yourself. Jason and LELDF were an answer to prayer for our family. That's because Brad and I aren't wealthy people. I run our family farm and Brad is a veteran turned cop. So I must ask you one of the toughest questions I've ever asked anyone. **[**Will you donate $35 or any amount to LELDF to help me save my husband?**](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z748occ29sr89ut789arg27gh9tc91ut0f4hpqo0_rp22sh2s8i6epj0spj60oj0clh2bs)** If I had anywhere else to turn, I wouldn't be so bold as to ask for your help. But I'm so scared for Brad and I will do whatever I can for him -- and for our sons. **[So I pray you'll find it in your heart today to make a tax-deductible gift of $35, $50, $100 or more to the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund.](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zst8crocr86fr6dsgfuce1ns9h08bpvav26j3n3o_rp22sh2s8i6epj0spj60oj0clh2bs) ** Brad and I -- and our two sons -- are counting on the good nature and generosity of kind neighbors like you to help keep Brad home where he belongs. No matter what you're able to give today, please pray for us. Thank you in advance for your support.

Sincerely,

Lacy Lunsford

| | To address this, we have created a new eBook, _**The History of Socialism and Capitalism**_ , authored by two of the most prominent voices in today's political discourse, Hoover Institution senior fellows Niall Ferguson and Victor Davis Hanson.

This new eBook offers a deep dive into the origins, development, and impacts of socialism and capitalism. Each scholar presents an in-depth analysis through two different lenses. It's hard to overstate the relevance of this eBook in today's policy debates, where radical proposals are gaining traction.

Understanding the historical and practical implications of socialism and capitalism is crucial for making informed decisions about our economic and political future. The insights provided by Ferguson and Hanson will equip you with the knowledge to critically evaluate these competing ideologies and their potential impact on society.

Don't miss this opportunity to enhance your understanding of these pivotal economic systems. subject: Who's Really in Charge?
body:
Here is some valuable info we are using to fight dark money in politics.
| | | | | | [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2w9so3-ukjkb4-kyd76rh5/)
---
# **So... Who's Really In Charge?**
---
| [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2w9so3-ukjkb5-kyd76rh6/)
---
| | | | friend, Politicians promise change, but too often, the status quo remains. The real question is: who’s truly in control? Is it the voters, or is it the shadowy interest groups flooding our elections with unlimited, undisclosed money? Dark money is the secret weapon of the wealthy few, and it’s time we pay attention.
**What is Dark Money?** Dark money refers to political donations that hide their source. Unlike most donations, dark money flows from politically active nonprofits and LLCs, which are not required to disclose their donors. This means we have no way of knowing who’s really funding political campaigns, leaving voters in the dark about who’s pulling the strings.
**How Does Dark Money Work?** Dark money is funneled through nonprofits and LLCs, often in states with loose regulations. These funds are used to run ads and influence campaigns—without revealing who’s behind them. This creates a system where the public has no insight into who’s shaping our elections.
**Why Does Dark Money Matter?** Dark money is poisoning our democracy. It allows corporations and wealthy elites to influence elections without accountability. Voters deserve transparency, but as long as dark money thrives, our political system is hijacked by those who can afford to keep their identities hidden. History proves that secret donations are a formula for corruption.
**Who Benefits?** The ones defending dark money are the very ones benefiting from it—corporations and the ultra-wealthy. They argue for anonymity, but this only protects their ability to manipulate elections without consequence.
**What Can We Do?** While tracking dark money is difficult, watchdogs like AIPAC Tracker continue to expose the influence of these secret donations. We can push for transparency, but we also need to focus on local elections where we can make a real impact. Education is key—when we understand the corrupt systems in place, we can fight back. [**_It's time to reclaim our democracy. Let’s stand up to dark money and ensure that the voices of the many, not the few, are heard. Together, we can make a difference._**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2w9so3-ukjkb6-kyd76rh7/)

## Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?
[YES](https://links.defend-the-constitution.org/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=2f9e76f1e2be49ed9e3aaf80f1e16bd8&_e=SspjYGiGzhPmGmIu3yAYF5Ic2ErdQL39g7xurtx0rHBRD3URWOwEHAN2oa537YQNcV9E3lHs4Cf_oAApt8CY_8_wBezajLFE4N0d9gfhqFDYqu4Wo75aGYIGaMRNd4jqoczYnRoKFfMyhroknHPD-J_0-NKtyetmdDCJT3lZXKJ67e9eo0OmzbgdPVMvnp7Aq-yq2hRNAXTi54PEos7rD4M2EBVcWfguyLTmMqyZ6IeE_s1R-gE_8_vPhuczxsat1srni6lUOl_1JbYI2X5S8MOlEEbC2tM5xBxqiNaYxkRydFkzGl-z0nF3DFdjvB8Wtx-D7O_Qqfw8xybwfCysP9mEgzeXlNKKkmr803SfsAgBUHFfOfrXuK85HvBim7TTQ22Xem7L_ZrlSkxOiCwsCK6pkPI4C3Q4c7R9GctbymQ%3D) [NO](https://links.defend-the-constitution.org/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=2f9e76f1e2be49ed9e3aaf80f1e16bd8&_e=SspjYGiGzhPmGmIu3yAYF5Ic2ErdQL39g7xurtx0rHBRD3URWOwEHAN2oa537YQNcV9E3lHs4Cf_oAApt8CY_8_wBezajLFE4N0d9gfhqFDYqu4Wo75aGYIGaMRNd4jqoczYnRoKFfMyhroknHPD-J_0-NKtyetmdDCJT3lZXKJ67e9eo0OmzbgdPVMvnp7Aq-yq2hRNAXTi54PEos7rD4M2EBVcWfguyLTmMqyZ6IeE_s1R-gE_8_vPhuczxsat1srni6lUOl_1JbYI2X5S8FEnyr6ibYluhgAAr8dj8l4DyIYlWIx9IEl5yRpPXTEOKRDbYYqDfAfM2xZwX7PIPVdYU_uffoZGkWEXR4VoySjRpPJohCohWsLE4tk2s-qWf0qKkPoJtXtSoI8u6oI-GyC3zdbvYosN5i4i_-1S0R8%3D) Dear Fellow American, I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter. **Good morning!** On this day in 1872, Republican governor E. J. Davis was [indicted by a grand jury](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GurCAQxvGngU7DMKNgQXEbu73tKc24oJKgbJSs69ufuP2p_tX3S76fx_DgmOI2_-c1uPKZ8qCVbioFFcLgOaZrIOndqHwHMjgwaFEjkpGLY2u0BaIRvGlobEhj1zGYVoFvgg8yuhtTgACAiFCTZf8kolaPU8fWClLBx5L3uiyhhA8fU7ryO-z1M68yuaWU1yHwn9C90P15nnU5Fs5biluo8z4L3X9XleerGq87QvdhK_tdY5XcnX-dMaV4tEaQmleO6YuXP9--nf4NAAD__848VhM) for invalidating the election results for the Third Congressional District in an effort to seat the Republican candidate, William T.
